name: Kaili, Ledo
catalog_quote: 4. Stress in Ledo always falls on the next to last syllable, and shifts with the attachment of suffixes and single syllable particles. From banua 'house' (stress on u) are thus formed: banuáku 'my house,' banuámu 'your house,' banuána 'his house, her house,' also 'their house,' banuáta 'our house' ... banua kámi 'id.' ... banua míu 'your (pl.) house,'

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage (Esser 1934 §I.4, orig. p.5) is present verbatim in the held Sulang translation at lines 290-296, and the supplementary long-vowel sentence at lines 321-322; footnote 9 (Bugis origin, relic form niulina) and the fast-speech diphthong note (kamáimo, kaláuna; careful speech ka-ma-í-mo) are also there and do not disturb a fixed: penultimate syllable/word coding (enclitic -ku/-mu/-na/-ta shift stress; disyllabic kami/miu are separate words; final long vowels count as two syllables). (2) Deciding source: a 1934 grammar sketch inside a learner's manual by a professional linguist; StressTyp2 uses the same source, so database and catalog are not independent.
